text:
Alex: Quick question — I'd like to propose a minimal version-binding surface for pins so clients can send a tiny hint to the router. Keep it small, predictable. Thoughts?
Maria: Sounds good, can you sketch the minimal fields?
Alex: Draft idea: a compact set: model_ref (opaque id), variant (optional), pin_v (schema version), soft_ttl (seconds), rollout_stage. Avoid full provenance blobs on request path. Example: 
```json
{
  "model_ref": "m-3a9f",
  "variant": "q4",
  "pin_v": 1,
  "soft_ttl": 3600,
  "rollout_stage": "canary"
}
```
Samir: +1 on small set. Reservation: prefer canonical stable id for model_ref (not content hash) so we don't force clients to compute hashes.
Ingrid: We also need telemetry fields to tie pins to rollout metrics. Suggest rollout_id and telemetry_sample_rate. But header size is a constraint.
Alex: True. Tradeoff: headers route faster through edge but are limited in size. Options: short header for routing with minimal fields, and a separate POST /pin to attach full metadata asynchronously.
Maria: Ops note — runtime hot path mustn't parse big blobs. If clients send provenance, we should accept a provenance_id only on request path and fetch the heavy record offline.
Samir: Backcompat: runtime must ignore unknown fields. Also add explicit schema version (pin_v) so we can evolve without breaking older clients.
Ingrid: For rollback behavior we need an explicit lock flag. If hard_lock=true, then router should not fallback to other variants — fail fast. Otherwise allow graceful fallback.
Alex: Proposed canonical minimal surface fields: model_ref, pin_v, variant (opt), soft_ttl, rollout_stage, rollout_id (short), telemetry_sample_rate (opt), hard_lock (opt), provenance_id (opt). Everything else lives off-path.
Maria: How should we encode in headers? Base64 of compact JSON? Or a tiny binary map?
Samir: Base64 JSON is simplest to start with; implementors won't choke. If perf demands, we can iterate to a binary CBOR-like map. Important: keep keys short to save bytes.
Alex: Example header name: x-rd-pin: base64url(zlib(json))). We'll include parsing fallback for uncompressed base64 JSON.
Ingrid: Migration plan: pin_v=0 => legacy behaviour (ignore binding), pin_v=1 => new router honors fields. Rollout: console will set x-rd-pin for canaries then we monitor.
Maria: Telemetry: rollout_id should be included in request traces and metrics. telemetry_sample_rate should be advisory — routers should sample independently but attach the hint to logs.
Samir: Also add a per-tenant max header size guard on the edge; reject oversized pins with 400 and return a short error pointing to /pin upload flow.
Alex: Agreed. Action items: I will draft RFC PR with encoding examples and perf numbers. Samir to prototype decode path in router. Ingrid to add telemetry schema and sampling guidance. Maria to add ops playbook for oversized pins and provenance uploads.
Maria: One more: we should document retention of provenance_id references (TTL) and how long console can keep them. Ops wants a default 30d then manual checkpoint for longer archives.
Alex: Noted — include that in RFC. I'll open the branch today.
deploy-bot: Deployed pin-parser change to staging at 1718460000 :rocket:
Alex: Great, I'll run integration tests against staging after the PR lands. Thanks everyone.
